title: Cerberus - Network Guardrails & Telemetry Scrub
summary: Deep dive on VPC/on-prem network guardrails, egress controls and telemetry requirements for SOC2 readiness. Discussed RBAC/SSO integrations, KMS key custody modes, audit log retention, and a lightweight smoke test for egress failover. Agreement to share hardened network template, packet capture guidance, and telemetry schema; pilot to run in staging for two weeks.
topics: VPC isolation and explicit egress proxies
On‑prem airgap vs controlled egress bridge
KMS key custody (customer vs Redwood) and HSM options
Audit log format & retention for SOC 2
RBAC + SAML SSO mapping and session lifetime
Traffic allowlists, reverse proxies, and IDS/IPS telemetry
action_items: Aisha Khan - Share 'Redwood private network hardened template' + sample helm values - 2027-01-18
Ben Torres - Prepare perf-safe KV cache test harness and short runbook for KV cache warmup - 2027-01-20
Marco Silva - Provide Cerberus staging CIDR ranges and proxy egress/bastion details - 2027-01-14
Tara Gupta - Confirm required audit log retention window and export destinations (S3/GCS/FTP) - 2027-01-15
next_steps: Redwood to send hardened network diagram + example iptables/iptables-nft rules
Customer to whitelist staging CIDRs and stand up egress proxy in staging environment
Schedule 30-min telemetry alignment call next week to finalize log schema
Start 2-week pilot in staging once whitelisting complete
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-01-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE); Ben Torres (Redwood SE); Samir Patel (Redwood); Liam O'Neill (CISO - Cerberus); Priya Menon (Head of Infra - Cerberus); Marco Silva (Network Eng - Cerberus); Tara Gupta (Compliance)

Summary: quick security and compliance scrub focused on private/VPC and on-prem guardrails, ingress/egress, telemetry, and KMS custody tradeoffs.

Topics: VPC isolation, egress proxies, soc two (sic) audit logs, RBAC SSO mapping, KMS custody, IDS/IPS telemetry, segmentation, canary fallback behavior.

00:00:12 - Aisha Khan: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, uh we'll try to keep it focused — main goals are to make sure the network isolation pattern matches your compliance needs and that observability covers audit events.
00:00:29 - Liam O'Neill: yeah thanks, quick note -- we're aiming for SOC 2 in Q2 and need clear evidence for network egress controls and log provenance.
00:00:39 - Ben Torres: great, can you confirm current topology in staging? is it fully on‑prem or hybrid with a VPC transit layer?
00:00:51 - Priya Menon: it's hybrid; most control plane is in our VPC but we do have an onprem cluster in a co-lo that handles PII transforms. we want the Redwood private control plane inside our VPC, and for the inference nodes to be air-gapped-ish, i mean controlled egress only.
00:01:10 - Marco Silva: to add, we recently locked down egress to an egress proxy and a few allowed destinations. but we need to validate that Redwood's callbacks and telemetry won't try to reach back to random endpoints.
00:01:26 - Aisha Khan: totally, so common pattern we recommend is explicit egress proxy + static IPs (staging CIDRs) plus a short list of allowed FQDNs; Redwood will provide a CSR of IPs for staging and prod. note: we do have a 'dedicated' mode and a "private control plane" option — apologies if I say Redwood Dedicate or Redwood Private weirdly, I'm saying it fast.
00:01:50 - Ben Torres: just to flag, our runtime uses KV cache and prefix caching which does open a short-lived outbound for telemetry and for model artifact fetches. we can pin artifact endpoints to your egress proxy. sometimes the transcript reads KV cash instead of KV cache in our docs, sorry.
00:02:10 - Tara Gupta: for audit logs, we need immutable provenance. can you support streaming logs to our central log cluster and also export tamper-evident copies to our S3 with KMS envelope encryption?
00:02:24 - Samir Patel: yes, we support streaming syslog/JSON events to HTTPS endpoints, and we can also ship to S3/GCS with signed manifests. the KMS custody options are: customer-managed keys (recommended for high-compliance), Redwood-managed keys (easier) or HSM-backed BYOK.
00:02:44 - Liam O'Neill: HSM sounds preferable, whats the latency or perf hit?
00:02:49 - Ben Torres: negligible for token-level encryption ops; the bigger ops are key unwraps at startup, but we do caching. for inference we don't encrypt model tensors in-flight beyond TLS. if you require additional encryption at rest that's a configuration we can enable.
00:03:10 - Priya Menon: on RBAC/SSO, we need SAML mapping to groups and support for short session lifetimes — 1 hour max for console and API keys rotate daily ideally.
00:03:22 - Aisha Khan: we have SAML + SCIM for group sync. session lifetime can be configured; API tokens can be rotated via automation, and audit events for token issuance are emitted. we'll share the SAML attribute mapping guide.
00:03:36 - Marco Silva: can we talk about ingress / egress rules? specifically, we want to avoid any NATting that would break source IP preservation for IDS logs.
00:03:45 - Ben Torres: we can support preserving original source via our egress proxy in passthrough mode, or you can terminate TLS at the proxy. if you need source IPs for network IDS correlation you'll want passthrough and mutual TLS between your proxy and our nodes.
00:04:03 - Liam O'Neill: mutual TLS is good. does Redwood provide client cert rotation or do we manage certs?
00:04:09 - Samir Patel: we offer both modes: Redwood-managed cert rotation or customer-managed certs with rotation script support. there's a small ops overhead if you manage certs, but it's doable.
00:04:22 - Aisha Khan: quick clarification: when we say private control plane we mean customer network-hosted control plane with an outbound-only egress to Redwood artifact repo or to your allowed endpoints — for air-gapped we do an on-prem package and manual artifact sync.
00:04:38 - Priya Menon: we might need the on-prem package for production, but for the pilot staging hybrid is fine.
00:04:45 - Ben Torres: ok, pilot checklist: whitelist staging CIDRs, stand up egress proxy, enable telemetry endpoint we provide, and we'll run a short KV cache warmup test to demonstrate safe behavior.
00:05:01 - Marco Silva: what's in the telemetry? we need to capture request id, user id mapping, model version, route, decision/ fallback events and error codes for forensics.
00:05:14 - Samir Patel: standard events include request_id, timestamp, route, model_id, model_version, latency_ms, outcome, error_code, and optional payload hashes. we can add custom tags like internal_user_id. logs are JSON and signed with a manifest for tamper evidence.
00:05:36 - Tara Gupta: retention - SOC 2 asks for a year, but some customers want seven years. can you keep long-term backups to our archive bucket?
00:05:47 - Aisha Khan: we can export to your archive bucket; retention policies are customer-controlled. Redwood retains operational logs for 90 days by default but can extend with add-on. we'll include pricing for long-retention.
00:06:03 - Liam O'Neill: how about IDS/IPS integration? can we stream full pcap or only metadata?
00:06:11 - Ben Torres: full pcap is heavy; we usually recommend metadata + occasional packet capture on demand. for the pilot we can capture short PCAP snippets and share them securely.
00:06:24 - Priya Menon: what about egress fallback if the proxy fails? we can't have uncontrolled egress.
00:06:31 - Ben Torres: fallback policy: if egress proxy is unreachable, nodes will drop outbound attempts and switch to local stub responses for non-critical fetches; for model-serving traffic, we fail closed unless you opt-in for a limited emergency outbound pool (needs approval).
00:06:48 - Marco Silva: that fail-closed behavior is critical for us. can you demonstrate it in the pilot?
00:06:53 - Aisha Khan: yes, pilot will include a simulated proxy outage test and we'll capture telemetry showing fail-closed events and audit entries.
00:07:02 - Liam O'Neill: on encryption and KMS, who has access to master keys in the customer-managed keys mode?
00:07:09 - Samir Patel: customer controls the KMS; Redwood only gets a wrapped key during startup via the KMS API. we never store unwrapped keys. HSM option means KMS connects to HSM and Redwood gets a sealed token that requires attestation.
00:07:24 - Tara Gupta: do you support key rotation without service disruption?
00:07:28 - Ben Torres: yes, hot rotation is supported; we stage the new key, rewrap, and switch over with no inference interruption. we emit audit events for key rotations.
00:07:40 - Priya Menon: we also need to ensure that audit logs for admin actions are immutable and show the SAML user mapping.
00:07:47 - Samir Patel: admin actions are logged with SAML subject and group attributes; we can include SCIM group id as well. logs are write-once to the streaming endpoint and can be backed by append-only storage.
00:08:01 - Aisha Khan: quick pause — any blockers from your side to start the pilot?
00:08:07 - Marco Silva: I need the CIDRs and a sample HAProxy config for egress.
00:08:12 - Aisha Khan: noted. Ben will take the HAProxy hint and sample rules.
00:08:16 - Ben Torres: i'll include example iptables-nft and haproxy front-end config — we'll also show mutual TLS artifacts.
00:08:24 - Liam O'Neill: curious on observability — can you produce a canonical telemetry schema we can ingest into Splunk?
00:08:31 - Samir Patel: yes, JSON schema + mapping for Splunk/Elastic + a sample ingestion pipeline. we'll share an initial draft.
00:08:41 - Priya Menon: about data residency, some data (customer PII) must stay in EU. can Redwood pin model artifacts and logs to eu-west region only?
00:08:52 - Aisha Khan: yes, region pinning is supported for hosted or dedicated; for private deployments you control the physical hosting region. for hybrid we'll ensure artifacts are pulled from eu region and logs persist in your eu bucket.
00:09:07 - Marco Silva: any pre-signed URLs or artifacts that could leak internal hostnames?
00:09:12 - Ben Torres: we use signed URLs with short TTL and notry, but we'll scrub hostnames in manifests if that's a must.
00:09:21 - Tara Gupta: what's the format of the tamper-evident manifest? SHA256 sums and a signed manifest?
00:09:26 - Samir Patel: yes sha256 for artifacts and a signed manifest with a timestamp and signature using Redwood's key; if you use BYOK we sign with customer key optionally.
00:09:39 - Aisha Khan: ok i'll recap. Redwood will: share hardened network template, provide staging ip ranges, send SAML attribute mapping, share telemetry schema and Splunk mapping, and include a short runbook for the proxy outage test.
00:09:55 - Liam O'Neill: thanks, when can we get the docs?
00:09:58 - Aisha Khan: i'll send the initial packet by EOD Monday — but ben will assemble the runbook and samir the telemetry schema over the week.
00:10:08 - Ben Torres: will do, and marco you'll send us the staging CIDRs.
00:10:13 - Marco Silva: yes i'll get that by Friday.
00:10:18 - Tara Gupta: one more question — for compliance evidence, can you provide signed logs showing admin action history for the last 90 days during the pilot?
00:10:26 - Samir Patel: yes, we can export signed admin logs and provide a validators script to verify manifests.
00:10:33 - Priya Menon: ok perfect. any blockers on SOC 2 controls that we should be worried about?
00:10:38 - Aisha Khan: nothing major; it's mostly configuration and evidence collection. we'll provide an artifacts checklist aligned to common SOC 2 criteria.
00:10:47 - Liam O'Neill: sounds good. can we book the telemetry alignment call for next Tuesday?
00:10:52 - Aisha Khan: yes i'll propose times after the call.
00:10:56 - Ben Torres: quick note — we'll include a short perf-safe KV cache warmup test plan so you can see latency behavior under the egress proxy.
00:11:06 - Marco Silva: thanks, that answers a lot.
00:11:10 - Aisha Khan: any final questions?
00:11:12 - Tara Gupta: none here.
00:11:14 - Liam O'Neill: all good, thanks.

(remaining 50 minutes were Q&A and clarifications; captured key sections above and a few mis-transcriptions where 'Redwood Dedicated' appeared as 'Redwood Dedicate' and KV cache as 'KV cash')

Closing (00:61:30): Aisha Khan: thanks everyone we'll follow up with the artifacts and pilot proposal; action items and next steps shared in the notes.
